column3: The immediately preceding prayer to avert Hell frames the same devoted household whose final prayer asks for spouses, offspring, and righteous leadership.
Abraham asks for sound judgment and inclusion among the righteous, supporting the focus's aspiration that family joy mature into a righteous public role.
The prayer joins offspring with steadfast prayer, a close precursor to asking that descendants become a source of settled joy and guidance.
It asks that descendants become a submitting community, closely aligning family continuity with the focus's God-conscious communal leadership.
The adjacent description of Hell sharpens the pious household's preceding request for protection before the focus's prayer.
Descendants receive prophethood and scripture, a direct instance of family continuity extending into enduring guidance.
Its believing speakers pray for forgiveness and protection from the Fire, a broad devotional parallel without the family or leadership dimension.
Zechariah's plea not to remain alone prepares the answered family restoration that closely illuminates the focus's request for spouse and offspring.
Guidance spreads through a named lineage, directly exemplifying descendants as an enduring religious good rather than mere biological succession.
A later believing community prays for itself and earlier believers, faintly echoing the focus's wish for a righteous community beyond the household.
The immediate warning of multiplied, humiliating punishment supplies the moral contrast to the focus's portrait of the devoted servants.
The drink from a spring does not clarify spouse, offspring, settled joy, or leadership.

The prayer gathers righteous fathers, spouses, and descendants into the Garden, closely paralleling the focus's household hope.

Mercy is assigned to those who have taqwa, offering only a general connection to the focus's intended community.

Zechariah receives the announcement of Yahya, a child who confirms truth and is righteous, supporting the focus's desire for blessed descendants.

The command to live with wives honorably gives a concrete ethical form to the focus's positive invocation of spouses.

The leaders of disbelief form a direct negative contrast to the focus's requested leadership for the God-conscious.
Sarah receives Isaac and then Jacob as glad tidings, presenting descendants as a divinely bestowed family blessing.
Divine blessing is pronounced upon Abraham's household, reinforcing the focus's household-centered prayer.
Joseph is taught and God's favor is completed upon the house of Jacob, connecting family succession with learned guidance.
The righteous enter the Gardens with righteous fathers, spouses, and descendants, the closest omitted parallel to the focus's integrated household hope.
Messengers are explicitly given wives and descendants, directly locating prophetic guidance within family life.
Abraham settles part of his offspring by the Sacred House so that they establish prayer, closely joining descendants to enduring worship.
God makes spouses, children, and grandchildren, directly naming the family gifts for which the focus gives thanks in prayerful form.
Children are restored as part of communal strengthening, a limited parallel to descendants as a collective good.
Every people are called with their imam, directly showing the communal consequence of the leadership requested in the focus.
A righteous father's integrity preserves a treasure for his two sons, showing how parental righteousness can protect a later generation.
Zechariah asks for a successor who will inherit his religious household, directly joining offspring with faithful continuity.
Yahya is announced as a divinely named son, continuing the narrative of an extraordinary, prayerful gift of offspring.

God grants Abraham Isaac and Jacob and makes each righteous, closely matching the focus's desire for descendants who are a source of good.
The community is commanded to arrange marriage for the unmarried righteous, directly supporting the focus's positive treatment of spouses.

Job receives back his family and their like with them as mercy, presenting restored family as a divine gift.
